item.title: Oracle SQL: Efficiently Search for Values Across All Tables and Columns
item.description:
“Oracle SQL: Efficiently Search for Values Across All Tables and Columns”

When faced with the task of locating a particular piece of data across your entire Oracle database, especially when the exact table and column are unknown, a systematic approach is crucial. Directing a broad search requires careful construction of SQL or PL/SQL statements to query metadata and then dynamically execute checks.

Initial Approach: Querying Metadata

A common starting point involves querying Oracle’s data dictionary views to identify candidate tables and columns. The ALL_TAB_COLUMNS view is instrumental here, providing details about all columns accessible to the current user.

item.title: Dynamic PIVOT in Oracle SQL: Strategies and Solutions
item.description:
“Dynamic PIVOT in Oracle SQL: Strategies and Solutions”

When working with relational databases, transforming rows into columns is a common requirement, often achieved using the PIVOT clause in SQL. However, situations arise where the columns you need to pivot on are not fixed and can change based on data. This is where dynamic pivoting becomes essential. This post delves into various approaches to tackle dynamic pivoting in Oracle SQL, presenting multiple accepted solutions with practical code examples.
